mainTopic: The מגרש as a 'quarter' of the תחום, and the משנה's dispute about adding a קרפף to a city
overview: The amud opens by checking the ברייתא's claim that the מגרש around a Levite city is one quarter (רביע) of the תחום. The plain arithmetic gives 8 out of 24, which is a third, so the גמרא offers three ways to reach a quarter: the city is round, רבינא says the מגרש is only along the sides, and רב אשי says it is only at the corners. רבינא objects that the פסוק says סביב, and רב אשי answers from the עולה, where 'around' means the corners. Next, רב חביבי and רב חנילאי from מחוזא challenge the round-city calculation, about jutting corners and about the 800 figure. רב אשי answers that the squaring is only imagined, and that the diagonal adds more than a quarter. A new משנה then brings a dispute about the קרפף: רבי מאיר adds one to every city, while the חכמים use it only to join nearby cities, including three villages in a triangle. In the גמרא, רבא finds the source in 'מקיר העיר וחוצה', and רב הונא and חייא בר רב disagree whether two cities get two strips or one. The סיפא of the משנה supports רב הונא, and חייא בר רב's defense continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Calculating the size of the open space: eight units
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds up the מגרש: 4 units along the sides plus 4 units at the corners, for 8 units in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take out the four squares along the sides and the four squares at the corners. How much is that? Eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its arithmetic. It counts how many 1,000-by-1,000 squares the מגרש takes up. The answer is eight. This number is setting up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Around a 1,000-by-1,000 city, a 1,000-אמה strip of מגרש covers four side squares and four corner squares. That makes 8 units, out of a total of 24 units for the whole תחום outside the city. The גמרא now has a number it can compare against the word 'רביע'.

keyTerms.meaning: Take away / set aside (in a calculation)
Here: the strips along the sides of the city
Corners: the squares diagonal to the city's corners

phrases.english: Take out four of the side strips
phrases.notes: Four squares of 1,000×1,000, one on each side of the city

phrases.english: and four of the corners.
phrases.notes: Four corner squares of 1,000×1,000

phrases.english: How much is that? Eight.
phrases.notes: Eight units (millions of square אמות) of מגרש

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the arithmetic that began on the previous amud, where the total תחום was found to be 24 units.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מגרש of a square city covers 8 units (4 sides plus 4 corners).

steps.title: Challenge: that is a third, not a quarter
steps.stepSummary: 8 out of 24 is one third. So how can the ברייתא call the מגרש a quarter?
steps.simpleTranslation: That's a third!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks. The numbers show that the מגרש is one third of the תחום, but the ברייתא said one quarter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 8 divided by 24 equals one third. The math seems to contradict the ברייתא's word 'רביע', so the ברייתא needs an explanation.

phrases.english: It is a third!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of step 1 to challenge the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the מגרש is רביע (one quarter) of the תחום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The arithmetic gives 8 out of 24, which is 1/3, not 1/4.

steps.title: Answer: the city is round, so the open space shrinks to a quarter
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a round city. A circle is a quarter smaller than a square, so the מגרש is 6 units, and 6 out of 24 is a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think it was said about a square city? It was said about a round city. By how much is a square bigger than a circle? By a quarter. Take away a quarter, and six are left. And six out of twenty-four is a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא was talking about a round city. Once we take away the extra corners, the מגרש is exactly one quarter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the גמרא's rule that a square is bigger than a circle by a quarter, the 8 units of מגרש shrink by 2, leaving 6. The 24 units of the תחום stay the same, because the תחום is measured as a square (as רש"י explains). So 6 out of 24 is one quarter, and the ברייתא is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: A square is bigger than a circle

steps.confusionAlert: Only the מגרש is reduced from 8 to 6. The total of 24 stays unchanged. Do not shrink both numbers, or the math will not work.

phrases.english: Do you think it was said about a square city?
It was said about a round city.

phrases.aramaic: כַּמָּה מְרוּבָּע יָתֵר עַל הֶעָגוֹל — רְבִיעַ,
phrases.english: By how much is a square bigger than a circle? By a quarter.
phrases.notes: Based on the rule that the circumference of a circle is three times its diameter

phrases.english: Take away a quarter, and six are left.
And six out of twenty-four
is a quarter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ בְּרִבּוּעָא קָאָמַר? בְּעִיגּוּלָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the ברייתא refers to a round city, not a square one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed a square city, so the מגרש was 8 units, which is 1/3.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a round city the מגרש is 6 units, which is exactly 1/4 of 24.

steps.title: רבינא: a quarter, with open space only along the sides
steps.stepSummary: רבינא keeps the city square and says the מגרש is only along the sides, not at the corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: What does 'a quarter' mean? A quarter of the side strips.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a different answer. The city can stay square, but the מגרש is given only along the sides of the city, not in the corners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא reads the case differently: the corners get no מגרש. According to one calculation, if you look only at the side strips, the מגרש comes out to exactly one quarter of the total. So 'רביע' is true without needing a round city.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of the side areas

phrases.english: Ravina said:
What is 'a quarter'? A quarter of the side strips.
phrases.notes: מגרש only along the sides, not at the corners

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: מַאי רְבִיעַ, רְבִיעַ דִּתְחוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of step 2, instead of the round-city answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining where the מגרש lies: only along the sides.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מגרש includes both the sides and the corners, so it comes out to 1/3.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מגרש is only along the sides, so it is a quarter, even for a square city.

steps.title: רב אשי: a quarter, with open space only at the corners
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the opposite of רבינא: the מגרש is only at the corners, and there it is a quarter of the area.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What does 'a quarter' mean? A quarter of the corners.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a third answer. The מגרש is given only in the corners, and in that area it equals one quarter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each corner zone of the תחום is 2,000 by 2,000 אמות, which is 4 units. The מגרש takes 1,000 by 1,000 אמות of it, which is 1 unit. So the מגרש is a quarter of each corner zone: 4 units out of 16 in total.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of the corner areas

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא calls the מגרש 'רביע'. The plain math gives 1/3, so the גמרא offers three ways to reach a quarter. (1) The city is round. (2) רבינא: the מגרש is only along the sides. (3) רב אשי: the מגרש is only at the corners.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
What is 'a quarter'? A quarter of the corners.
phrases.notes: מגרש only at the corners: 1 unit out of each 4-unit corner zone

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מַאי רְבִיעַ, רְבִיעַ דִּקְרָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the same קשיא, the mirror image of רבינא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining where the מגרש lies: only in the corners.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מגרש includes both the sides and the corners, so it comes out to 1/3.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מגרש is only in the corners, where it is exactly 1/4 of the area.

steps.title: רבינא objects: the verse says around
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי: the פסוק says the מגרש is סביב, around the city, so how can it be only at the corners?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But the פסוק says 'around'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב אשי's idea from the previous step. That idea was that the מגרש is only at the corners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the ערי הלוים says the open space goes סביב, around the city. 'Around' sounds like every side of the city. So a corners-only מגרש seems to contradict the wording of the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is written! (a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But 'around' is written!
phrases.notes: Numbers 35:4. The open space goes around the city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's corners-only answer from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the מגרש is only at the corners
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's word סביב implies open space on all sides, not just at the corners.

steps.title: Around can mean around the corners, as with the altar
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that סביב means around the corners. He proves it from the עולה, whose blood goes 'around' the מזבח but is actually put only on its corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'around' mean? Around at the corners. If you do not say this, then by the עולה it is written, 'And they shall throw the blood on the מזבח around.' Would you say there too that it means literally all the way around? Rather, 'around' there means around the corners. Here too, 'around' means around the corners.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends himself. He shows that the תורה sometimes uses the word סביב to mean only the corners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the עולה, the blood is not smeared all around the מזבח. It is put only on the corners, and the תורה still calls that סביב. So the same word by the ערי הלוים can also mean the corners, and רב אשי's view fits the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: around by way of the corners
and they shall throw the blood

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common גמרא method: the same word is defined the same way in two places in the תורה.

phrases.english: What is 'around'? Around at the corners,
for if you do not say so,
regarding the burnt offering, where it is written:
'And (the sons of Aaron) shall throw the blood
phrases.notes: Leviticus 1:5

phrases.english: on the altar around,'
there too, is it literally all around?!
phrases.notes: Obviously not. The blood goes on the corners.

phrases.english: Rather, what is 'around'? Around at the corners;
here too: what is 'around'? Around at the corners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word in the פסוק by comparing it to another פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סביב means on every side of the city.
steps.terutzMaskana: סביב can mean at the corners, as it does by the עולה, so a corners-only מגרש fits the פסוק.

steps.title: רב חביבי asks about the jutting corners
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבי מחוזנאה challenges רב אשי on the round-city calculation (step 3). Cities are squared off for measuring, so the corners of that square jut into the 1,000-אמה open space and shrink it. That spoils the 'quarter' calculation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבי from מחוזא said to רב אשי: But there are the corners that stick out!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge is brought against רב אשי. If the city is square, its corners poke out into the area being measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The round-city answer assumed a full 1,000-אמה ring of מגרש around a circular city. But the city is measured as a square, and the corners of that square jut out into the ring. Those protrusions eat into the open space, so the 6-out-of-24 figure seems wrong.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חֲבִיבִי מָחוֹזְנָאָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Chavivi of Mechoza said to Rav Ashi:
But there are the protrusions of the corners!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the round-city answer of step 3 and challenges it from the rule that a city's boundary is always squared: the corners of the square jut into the open space.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that for a round city the מגרש comes out to exactly a quarter of the תחום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A square city's jutting corners take up part of the open space, so the numbers are off.

steps.title: We are dealing with a round city
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the case is a round city, which has no jutting corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about a round city.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers in just two words. The case is a circular city, so there are no corners poking out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A round city has no corner points that stick out. The problem of jutting corners therefore does not apply. This also connects back to the round-city answer from step 3.

phrases.english: With a round city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חביבי's challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a round city
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The city is square, with corners that stick out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The city is round, so nothing sticks out.

steps.title: But cities are always squared
steps.stepSummary: The challenger pushes back: the משנה says every city is squared off. So how can we treat it as round?
steps.simpleTranslation: But they squared it!
steps.whatsHappening: The answer of a round city is challenged. The rule is that we always square a city off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that even a round city is measured as if it were a square. If so, it seems the round city also ends up with corners. Then the jutting-corner problem comes right back.

phrases.english: But haven't they squared it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the round-city answer of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that we can treat the city as round
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of squaring a city seems to turn every city into a square, corners included.

steps.title: We only imagine it squared, we do not really square it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that squaring is only a way of looking at the city for measuring. The city does not actually become square, so the empty corner areas stay open space.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that we say: we look at it as if it were squared. Do we actually make it square?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי closes the challenge. He separates two things: measuring the city as a square, and actually treating it as a square.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Squaring is a measuring tool for the תחום. We imagine square lines around the round city. But the empty pieces between the circle and those imagined lines are not really city. So they still count as part of the open space.

keyTerms.meaning: we view it as if it were squared

steps.whatToRemember: Squaring a city is only a way of measuring. A round city stays round in reality, so the empty corner areas remain part of the מגרש.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the squaring rule adds land or houses to the city. It is only an imagined frame for measuring.

phrases.english: Granted that we say
we view it as if it were squared.
Do we actually, truly square it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the squaring challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing an imagined frame used for measuring from physical reality
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Squaring turns the city into a real square with corners.
steps.terutzMaskana: Squaring is only imagined for measuring, so the city stays round and the corner gaps remain open space.

steps.title: The numbers do not add up: a square is only a quarter bigger than a circle
steps.stepSummary: רב חנילאי מחוזנאה argues that the 800 figure is too big. If a square exceeds a circle by only a quarter, the answer should be 666⅔.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנילאי from מחוזא said to רב אשי: How much bigger is a square than a circle? By a quarter. So how do you get 800? It should only come to 667 minus a third!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenger attacks the math behind רב אשי's explanation. He says the extra area gained by squaring the city has been calculated too high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a square is a quarter bigger than the circle inside it. If you use that rule, the extra area from squaring the round city comes to 666⅔, not the 800 that was stated earlier. So the earlier number seems to be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now, look' (opens a logical point that everyone accepts)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חֲנִילַאי מָחוֹזְנָאָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥanilai from Meḥoza said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדִי כַּמָּה מְרוּבָּע יָתֵר עַל הֶעָגוֹל —
phrases.english: Now, by how much is a square larger than a circle?
By a quarter.
phrases.notes: An accepted math rule: a circle is three-quarters of the square drawn around it.

phrases.english: So are these eight hundred?
phrases.notes: That's the 800 from the math a moment ago.

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁית מְאָה וְשִׁיתִּין וּשְׁבַע נָכֵי תִּילְתָּא הָוֵי!
phrases.english: It is only six hundred sixty-seven minus a third!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חֲנִילַאי מָחוֹזְנָאָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי מִכְּדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new mathematical challenge to the calculation that רב אשי's explanation relies on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 800 figure for the area added when the round city is squared.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using the rule that a square is one quarter larger than a circle gives 666⅔, which contradicts the 800.

steps.title: The quarter rule does not cover the diagonal corners
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the quarter rule applies only to a circle inside a square. The corners are measured on the diagonal, which is 1 and 2/5 times the side, so more area is added.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That rule is only for a circle inside a square. But on the diagonal, we need more. As the Master said: every אמה on the side of a square is one אמה and two-fifths on its diagonal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the 800 figure. He explains that the challenger used the wrong rule for this shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'one quarter' rule only compares a circle with the square drawn tightly around it. Here the added corner space reaches out along the diagonal. A diagonal is about 1.4 times as long as a side, so the added area is bigger than a quarter. Once you count it this way, 800 is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: A circle set inside a square

steps.whatToRemember: Rule of thumb in the גמרא: the diagonal of a square equals its side plus two-fifths (1.4). That is why corners add more space than the simple 'quarter' rule suggests.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This applies only to a circle inside a square.
But on the diagonal, we need more.
As the Master said,
Every cubit on the side of a square
is a cubit and two-fifths on the diagonal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּעִיגּוּלָא מִגּוֹ רִבּוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the math challenge of step 12 and ends the calculation discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule the challenger relied on (it applies to a different shape).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The quarter rule covers all the extra area gained by squaring, so the answer is 666⅔.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra corners reach out along the diagonal (1 and 2/5 times the side), so the added area is larger and 800 is correct.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: every city gets an added קרפף
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. רבי מאיר rules that a קרפף strip is added to every city before the תחום שבת is measured.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We give a קרפף to a city. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's discussion ends and a new משנה opens. רבי מאיר says every city gets an extra strip of about 70 אמות around it before we start counting the 2000 אמות of the תחום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרפף here means a strip of 70 and two-thirds אמות. רבי מאיר says it is added to every city, even a city standing alone. So the תחום שבת is measured from the edge of this added strip, not from the last house.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: an added strip of about 70⅔ אמות around a city

steps.confusionAlert: Here קרפף does not mean a fenced enclosure, as it does elsewhere. It means a set measurement of empty space added to the city's edge.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One allocates a karpef to a city,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It changes the topic from squaring the city to adding a קרפף strip.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, every city gets an added קרפף of about 70⅔ אמות before the תחום is measured.

steps.title: חכמים: the קרפף only joins two nearby cities
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the קרפף applies only between two cities. If each has 70-plus אמות of space toward the other and these overlap, the two cities count as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: They only spoke of a קרפף between two cities. If this city has seventy אמות and a bit, and that city has seventy אמות and a bit, the קרפף makes the two of them into one.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. They say a city standing alone gets no קרפף. The קרפף only matters when two cities are close to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each city is given 70⅔ אמות toward the other. If the gap between them is no more than two of these strips (141⅓ אמות), the strips meet. Then the two cities are treated as one city, and the תחום is measured from the far edge of both.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
They did not speak of a karpef
except between two cities.

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לָזוֹ שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירַיִים
phrases.english: If this one has seventy cubits and a remainder
and that one has seventy cubits and a remainder,

phrases.aramaic: עוֹשֶׂה קַרְפֵּף אֶת שְׁתֵּיהֶן לִהְיוֹת אֶחָד.
phrases.english: the karpef makes the two of them into one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים לֹא אָמְרוּ קַרְפֵּף אֶלָּא בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion to רבי מאיר in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרפף is not added to a lone city. It only joins two cities whose 70⅔-אמה strips meet, so they count as one city.

steps.title: Three villages in a triangle are joined by the middle one
steps.stepSummary: The same idea applies to three villages in a triangle. If the two outer villages are within 141⅓ אמות of each other, the middle village joins all three into one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise with three villages set in a triangle: if there are 141⅓ אמות between the two outer ones, the middle one makes all three into one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה extends the חכמים's rule to a case with three villages. It shows that the middle village can link the two outer ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number 141⅓ is exactly two קרפף strips (70⅔ + 70⅔). In a triangle, the middle village sits out of line. We picture it as if it were placed in the gap between the outer two. If the gap is no more than 141⅓ אמות, the three villages count as one.
steps.whatToRemember: 141⅓ אמות is simply two קרפף strips of 70⅔. That is the largest gap that still lets villages be joined into one.

phrases.english: And likewise, three villages arranged in a triangle:
if there is between the two outer ones
one hundred forty-one and a third cubits,
the middle one makes all three of them
into one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the חכמים's rule about joining cities to a three-village triangle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the two outer villages of a triangle are within 141⅓ אמות of each other, the middle village joins all three into one for measuring the תחום.

steps.title: Where does the extra strip come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and asks for the source of רבי מאיר's rule that a קרפף is added to a city before measuring the תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section starts. It asks where in the תורה we learn that a strip of קרפף is added to a city before the תחום is measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated the rule but gave no source. The גמרא wants to know what this extra space is based on, since the תורה only speaks of 2000 אמות. This question sets up the next step, where רבא brings a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that comes after the משנה
From where are these things learned? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא starts talking about the new משנה.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He's asking where we learn that a קרפף gets added to the city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה quoted in steps 14-16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for adding a קרפף to a city before measuring the 2000 אמות of תחום.

steps.title: רבא's verse: give space outside, then measure
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the פסוק 'מקיר העיר וחוצה' and reads it as: first give some space outside the city, and only then measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says, 'from the wall of the city and outward.' The Torah is saying: first give some space outside, and only afterward measure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question with a פסוק about the cities of the לויים. He reads it as telling us to add space outside the wall first, and only then start measuring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וחוצה' ('and outward') sounds extra. רבא reads it as an instruction to set aside an outside strip, the קרפף, before the count begins. So the 2000 אמות are measured from the edge of that strip, not from the wall itself.

keyTerms.meaning: From the wall of the city and outward (במדבר ל״ה:ד)
Give outside: add a strip of space beyond the wall

phrases.english: Rava said:
For the verse says: 'From the wall of the city and outward.'
phrases.notes: Numbers 35:4, about the open land around the Levite cities.

phrases.english: The Torah said: give outside,
phrases.notes: First set aside a strip outside the wall.

phrases.english: and afterward measure.
phrases.notes: Only then begin counting the 2000 אמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'מקיר העיר וחוצה' teaches that a strip is given outside the wall first, and only then is the measurement made.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the קרפף has a source in the תורה (according to רבא's reading). It is not just an arbitrary addition.

steps.title: רב הונא: each city gets its own strip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים of the משנה and brings רב הונא's view: when two cities are near each other, each one receives its own קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the חכמים say: they only said...' It was stated: רב הונא said, we give a קרפף to this city and a קרפף to that city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the חכמים's opinion and introduces an argument between אמוראים about it. This step gives the first side, רב הונא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said the קרפף applies only between two cities. רב הונא explains that each city gets its own 70⅔-אמה strip. Together that allows a gap of 141⅓ אמות between the two cities for them to still count as one.

keyTerms.meaning: An enclosed open area. Here, a strip of 70⅔ אמות

phrases.english: 'And the Sages say: they only said, etc.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the משנה's second opinion to start a new topic.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Huna said:
We give a karpef to this city
and a karpef to that city.
phrases.notes: Two strips in total, 141⅓ אמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי מאיר's source to explaining the חכמים's opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Between two cities, each city gets its own קרפף, so the gap allowed totals 141⅓ אמות.

steps.title: חייא בר רב: one shared strip
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב disagrees. The two cities share only one קרפף between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב said: one קרפף for the two of them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the argument. חייא בר רב says the two cities get only one strip, which they share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this view, the total gap allowed between the cities is only 70⅔ אמות, not double that. The argument is about whether the קרפף is counted once per city or once per pair of cities.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two numbers. רב הונא allows a gap of 141⅓ אמות (two strips). חייא בר רב allows only 70⅔ אמות (one strip).

phrases.english: Chiyya bar Rav said:
One karpef for the two of them.
phrases.notes: A single shared strip of 70⅔ אמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב הונא in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two cities share one קרפף. The total gap allowed is 70⅔ אמות.

steps.title: The משנה says 'קרפף' in the singular
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from the משנה's wording, which mentions one קרפף between two cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'The חכמים say: they only said קרפף between two cities.' This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא. It uses the exact words of the משנה, which speak of 'a קרפף' (one) between two cities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to describe a single strip serving both cities. That matches חייא בר רב. It contradicts רב הונא, who gives each city its own strip, so the גמרא calls it a 'תיובתא', a strong refutation.

phrases.english: We learned: And the Sages say:
They only spoke of a karpef
phrases.notes: It says just one קרפף, which sounds like a single strip.

phrases.english: between two cities,
A refutation of Rav Huna!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא אָמְרוּ קַרְפֵּף אֶלָּא בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב הונא's view against the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that each city gets its own קרפף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says 'קרפף' in the singular for two cities, which implies one shared strip.

steps.title: 'קרפף' means the rule of קרפף
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that 'קרפף' in the משנה means 'the law of קרפף'. In fact each city gets its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can say to you: What does 'קרפף' mean? The rule of קרפף. Really, there is a קרפף for this city and a קרפף for that city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא. The singular word in the משנה is a name for the rule, not a count of how many strips there are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is only saying the קרפף concept applies between two cities. It is not telling us how many strips are given. So the wording no longer contradicts רב הונא, and his two-strip view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you: introduces a defense on someone's behalf

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא gives each city its own קרפף (141⅓ אמות total). חייא בר רב gives one shared קרפף. The משנה's singular 'קרפף' means 'the rule of קרפף', so it does not disprove רב הונא.

phrases.english: Rav Huna can say to you:
What is 'karpef'? The law of karpef,
phrases.notes: The word names the rule, not the number of strips.

phrases.english: and really, a karpef for this city
and a karpef for that city.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: מַאי קַרְפֵּף, תּוֹרַת קַרְפֵּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The singular 'קרפף' was taken to mean one physical strip shared by both cities.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'קרפף' means the legal concept of קרפף. Each city still receives its own strip.

steps.title: The end of the משנה supports רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from the סיפא of the משנה that each city receives its own קרפף of seventy אמות and a remainder, as רב הונא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it makes sense, because the end of the משנה teaches: if this city has seventy אמות and a little more, and that city has seventy אמות and a little more, the קרפף joins both cities to be one. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for רב הונא. It points to the last part of the משנה, which talks about each city having its own seventy אמות and a bit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא gives a separate seventy אמות and a remainder to this city and also to that city. If the two of them shared only one קרפף, there would be no reason to list the space for each city on its own. So the wording shows that each city has its own קרפף, which is exactly רב הונא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is reasonable (introduces a supporting proof)
The latter clause or end of a משנה
Seventy אמות and a remainder (two-thirds of an אמה), the size of a קרפף
An extra strip of area added around a city before measuring the תחום
Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof strengthens רב הונא's reading of the משנה. It also sets up the challenge against חייא בר רב that comes in the next step.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
phrases.notes: Introduces support for רב הונא

phrases.english: from the fact that the latter clause teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לָזוֹ שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירַיִים
phrases.english: if this city has seventy cubits and a remainder
and that city has seventy cubits and a remainder
phrases.notes: Each city is given its own measurement, which is the key point

phrases.english: the karpef is made for both of them
so that they become one.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב הונא's answer in step 22 that each city gets its own קרפף
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that each of two neighboring cities receives its own קרפף
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה, which assigns seventy אמות and a remainder to each city separately

steps.title: Is this a refutation of חייא בר רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the סיפא, which supported רב הונא, should be a decisive refutation of חייא בר רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that this is a refutation of חייא בר רב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the proof around. If the משנה supports רב הונא, it seems to knock down חייא בר רב, who said the two cities share only one קרפף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא gives each city its own seventy אמות and a remainder. That seems to clash directly with חייא בר רב's view of a single shared קרפף. The word תיובתא signals a very strong attack, an attempt to fully refute his position.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (proposes a conclusion that will be tested)
A decisive refutation of an אמורא's view from a תנאי source

steps.confusionAlert: The word לימא does not mean the refutation is final. It usually opens a suggestion that the גמרא is about to reject, as happens in the next step.

phrases.english: Let us say this is a refutation
of Chiyya bar Rav!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּחִיָּיא בַּר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the proof from step 23 to attack the opposing view of חייא בר רב
steps.kashyaTarget: חייא בר רב's view that two neighboring cities share one קרפף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא gives a separate seventy אמות and a remainder to each city, which contradicts the idea of one shared קרפף

steps.title: חייא בר רב begins his defense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces the answer that חייא בר רב would give. The content of the answer continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב could say to you:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is opening חייא בר רב's defense, and the actual explanation comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אמר לך means the speaker could reply this way, even if he never actually said it. So the גמרא is about to show that the סיפא can be read in a way that fits one shared קרפף.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (introduces a possible defense on someone's behalf)

phrases.english: Chiyya bar Rav could say to you:
phrases.notes: His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the response to the challenge in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defense of an אמורא against a refutation (content follows on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא seems to disprove חייא בר רב
steps.terutzMaskana: The explanation of how the סיפא fits one shared קרפף continues on the next amud (57b).
